findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence-ranked gene and its tumour transcripts sit almost entirely in RCC cells (share of tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]), with the percentage of RCC cells expressing it at [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7], so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic; the purity-adjusted bulk fold change stays large.

In paired donor pseudobulk, CA9 in tumour cells exceeds normal proximal tubule cells by [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]; in Visium, high-CA9 spots are significantly enriched for RCC neighbours and the composition-corrected expresser is RCC, with macrophage neighbours only weakly enriched.

The CA9 AlphaFold model has mean pLDDT [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; its top cavity has volume (A3) [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] with one nearby accessible lysine (K109), and cavities recover about half of experimental ligand-contact residues. This is a descriptive monomer heuristic only, not degron or ligase evidence; CA9 already has drugs (girentuximab, sulthiame) and no DepMap dependency.

CD70 has the strongest tumour-cell-directed profile after CA9: RCC cells are the largest per-cell source in scRNA, with a minority of Tregs and T cells also expressing it, TCGA replicates the increase and the pure-tumour extrapolation remains positive, but there is no DepMap dependency and no prognostic signal; clinical anti-CD70 agents already exist, so it is not first-in-class.

KDR is an endothelial gene, not a tumour-cell target: endothelium holds 0.951 of tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], and RCC cells are not among the expressing groups.

Despite being the HIF2A driver, EPAS1 transcripts in the scRNA are mainly stromal: the percentage of endothelial cells expressing it is [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3] versus only [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=4.9], so a bulk EPAS1 signal is not a clean tumour-cell readout (possibly partly a 10x dropout effect for a low-abundance transcription factor).

CD74 is an immune-cell gene: macrophages hold 0.436 of tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], with CD8 T cells also contributing because they are so numerous, and dendritic cells having the highest per-cell level. It is a microenvironment marker, not a tumour-cell target.

CXCR4 is carried by lymphocytes: CD8 T cells hold 0.563 of tumour transcripts [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], with CD4 T, B, Treg and pDC cells also expressing it, so it is an immune-axis target and not tumour-intrinsic.

NNMT ranks eighth in convergence with tumour-intrinsic and purity-robust signal, and in TCGA higher expression carries adverse survival (significant after correction in the ranking record); it has no clinical drug and no selective DepMap dependency, so it is a prognostic biomarker with an untested functional role. Cell attribution was not queried here.

COL23A1 is the top tumour-track candidate: RCC cells hold most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], the TCGA log2FC is [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; tcga_log2fc=5.829], the signal is purity-robust, there is no clinical drug and few ccRCC papers, UniProt places it at the cell membrane (SURFY says nonsurface, not seen in CSPA), vital-organ expression is low, and TCGA survival shows no adverse effect. Missing: dependency evidence (not selective), normal-tissue staining, intratumour heterogeneity; literature is counted by gene symbol.

The COL23A1 AlphaFold model is low confidence (mean pLDDT [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) and only one tiny shallow cavity was detected, with no ligand-site validation possible; this suggests antibody rather than small-molecule modality, and is a descriptive monomer result only.

RAB42 is a second tumour-track candidate: RCC cells hold the largest share of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], it replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust, with few ccRCC papers, no clinical drug and low vital-organ expression; however its surface location is unknown (an intracellular small GTPase is not antibody-accessible), DepMap shows no selective dependency and TCGA survival is not significant.

OLFML2A is a stroma-track candidate made by fibroblasts (share of tumour transcripts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]); it is secreted, replicated in TCGA, purity-robust, has few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, but it is expressed in colon (higher vital-organ signal), has no dependency evidence and is a microenvironment target.

JAG2 is an endothelial stroma-track candidate (share of tumour transcripts [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487]), a surface Notch ligand with CSPA support, replicated and purity-robust with no clinical drug; the lower endothelial share, more existing ccRCC literature, heart expression and lack of dependency data make it a weaker hypothesis, and TCGA survival is not adverse.

MILR1 is the top immune-track candidate (macrophage share of tumour transcripts [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.841]) with no ccRCC papers and a surface call; but its log2FC shrinks towards zero when extrapolated to a pure tumour and it is flagged infiltration_driven, so the bulk rise reflects macrophage abundance rather than tumour cells; TCGA survival is adverse and there is no clinical drug, bone marrow expression is a safety question.

LILRB4 is a macrophage-borne immune-track candidate (share of tumour transcripts [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.933]); it is a surface antibody-tractable checkpoint-like receptor with no clinical drug listed, but the pure-tumour extrapolation is small and the gene is infiltration_driven, survival is not significant and lung expression needs safety review.

caveats: Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; no selective DepMap dependency or functional evidence was found for any, and literature is counted by gene symbol.
Structural scores describe AlphaFold monomer cavities and say nothing about degrons, ligases or degradation.
scRNA covers 12 donors and some cell groups (endothelium, fibroblasts, proximal tubule) have few donors; low EPAS1 detection in RCC cells may reflect 10x dropout.

Spatial enrichment was run only for CA9; MET, EGFR, SCARB1, COXFA4L2 and ALDOB were not examined at cell level because of the tool budget; CD70, NNMT and COXFA4L2 findings rest partly on ranking records.
Several top-ranked down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, PIGR) are proximal tubule biomarkers of lost normal epithelium, not therapeutic targets.
